first_impression: I went in expecting a brainless cozy simulator, but this is an actual, honest-to-god sheepdog game with legitimate herding mechanics. The low-poly aesthetic is pretty standard indie fare, but the UI polish and authentic rural atmosphere immediately grabbed me.
best_things: It implements genuine sheepdog trials and handling tactics like creeping, flanking, and staring down rams instead of just bumping hitboxes around.
The seasonal structure introduces a new mechanical twist almost every single level, from floodwaters and mist to controlling Pip's mother Fly.
The night watch level flips the script into tense perimeter defense against wolves while the sheep sleep in balls.

worst_problems.problem: Wolf threats trigger mostly off-screen with sudden text alerts, forcing frantic camera scanning rather than deliberate spatial defense.
worst_problems.suggestion: Add an on-screen peripheral threat indicator pointing toward stalking wolves so you can react without losing sight of your flock.

worst_problems.problem: Camera perspective shifts drastically into low-angle third-person where tall grass completely obscures sheep and pathing.
worst_problems.suggestion: Keep the orthographic top-down view consistent or give player-controlled smooth zoom and pitch instead of sudden angle locks.

worst_problems.problem: The paper minimap looks nice on paper but lacks real-time contrast, making it hard to track scattered sheep against riverbanks at a glance.
worst_problems.suggestion: Increase the contrast on sheep dots and add faint trail lines showing where stragglers are heading.

worst_problems.problem: Sheep geometry looks like jagged crumpled paper that clashes with the smooth UI and soft skyboxes.
worst_problems.suggestion: Soft-shade the flock models slightly or give the wool texture a bit more fluff so they do not look like sharp low-poly rocks.

worst_problems.problem: Keybind prompts take up substantial screen real estate at the bottom-center throughout the entire playthrough.
worst_problems.suggestion: Fade the control bar into an optional HUD element or collapse it once past the opening two evenings.

boredom_points: Slow-walking behind stubborn sheep over long distances when you already have the flock oriented correctly toward the gate.
Trudging back and forth across empty pasture to pick up a single stray that panicked over a stream.
confusions: Whether the low-angle perspective in e1-low-view.jpg is a cinematic cut or an actual playable camera mode.
The exact aggro radius of wolves around Old Angus when he is guarding ewes.
wish_list: Customizable dog coats or collars earned via ribbon completion.
A procedural trial generator mode with custom gate layouts and timers for endless replayability.
Dynamic weather audio like roaring wind and pelting rain to match the storm visually.
one_line_review: An authentic, surprisingly tense border collie simulator that trades brainless cozy fluff for real herding discipline.
